lines.text: In 1925, a con artist named Mr. Victor Lustig pulled off the craziest scam in history.
He sold the entire Eiffel Tower... not once, but twice!
Back then, the Eiffel Tower was rusting badly in the dark Paris skies.
Newspapers reported that the city was thinking about tearing it down.
So under the cover of night, Mr. Lustig forged official French government credentials.
He called Paris's top scrap-metal dealers to a secret midnight meeting at the Hotel de Crillon.
In a dim, private suite, he whispered that the demolition was a top-secret state project.
And he opened private bids for seven thousand tons of scrap iron.
One wealthy dealer, Mr. André Poisson, was desperate to win the contract.
Until he suddenly grew suspicious: why was this meeting so secretive?
Sensing his hesitation, Mr. Lustig played his masterstroke:
he leaned in close... and quietly demanded a massive bribe.
Instantly, Mr. Poisson's doubts vanished.
He thought: a corrupt bureaucrat? This must be the real government!
So Mr. Poisson handed over a suitcase stuffed with cash...
and Mr. Lustig escaped on the midnight train to Vienna.
Now here's the craziest twist:
Mr. Poisson was so humiliated that he bought the Eiffel Tower...
he never said a single word to the police!
When Mr. Lustig saw zero headlines in the morning news,
he slipped right back into Paris under the moonlight,
and sold the Eiffel Tower all over again to another victim!
Because in the end, he was never selling iron...
he was selling human greed.
For more unbelievable true stories, follow NEXORA!
